prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a MACRO WORLD MAP CONCEPT of an ENORMOUS ORIGINAL FANTASY VIETNAMESE CAPITAL, THANG LONG, seen truly from above as a simplified pixel-art RPG city map. This must clearly look like a huge sprawling city with MANY neighborhoods and hundreds of SMALL BUILDING BLOCKS, NOT one market square or one gameplay screen. Large walled rectangular city, twelve distinct urban districts linked by wide north-south and east-west avenues, outer gates in four compass directions, an inner royal precinct in the north, huge bustling grand market east, forge and artisan wards southeast, guild ward southwest, western canal/harbor warehouses, residential garden courtyards, lakes and bridges, central grand civic/PVP arena square as just ONE small landmark within the immense capital. City fills almost entire landscape board; buildings tiny relative to total city. Clean readable 16-bit-style PIXEL GAME art, large simple stepped shapes, sparse texture, 3 colors per roof/stone/water material, limited warm red clay roofs, ivory stone, jade canal, moss-green trees, muted gold roofs for important landmarks only. Orthogonal top-down plan, not isometric perspective, not photorealistic or hand-painted HD illustration. Cohesive Vietnamese vernacular-inspired fantasy architecture, no copied real historic plan, no Forbidden City replica, no giant dragons everywhere. Add at bottom right a small framed inset showing a SINGLE street corner at gameplay scale with one tiny chibi sprite and 3 simple modular houses; a hairline rectangle somewhere in whole city indicates that inset is only a tiny fraction of the world. Clean hierarchy, map readability and scale. Only text allowed: THANG LONG at top, WORLD OVERVIEW and ONE STREET in small labels. No arbitrary numerical scale written. This is a visual world-planning concept, not approved runtime terrain geometry.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create a SIMPLE, VERY CRISP PIXEL GAME SCREEN for an original top-down Vietnamese-inspired fantasy RPG, beginner-manageable production quality, not a detailed illustrated painting. A single street CORNER inside an immense capital, shown at normal gameplay zoom, never the whole city. Think deliberate low-resolution source artwork at 320x180 logical pixels enlarged exactly4x with hard nearest-neighbor blocks to1280x720. Big visible square pixels, no subpixel features or smoothing. 16x16 tile grammar, flat color clusters, ONLY3 tones per material and around32 colors overall. Two small modular red-tile roof timber-and-plaster houses left and upper-right, one small market awning, clean pale stone path broad open center, a short jade-water canal on right with simple4-frame-style ripple marks, one tiny square bridge, TWO stylized chunky trees, four simple pots/crates total, very sparse ground texture. One chibi courier with blue coat/ochre trim and brown bag, and one blue-haired crimson-cape hero at source size32x40 maximum, readable separated feet. Character sizes and houses match a cozy game, not realistic proportions. Orthographic top-down camera, north up. Warm friendly daylight; strong silhouette contrast, ink navy outline1source pixel, clear roof blocks, no individually rendered roof shingles, no thousands of grass speckles, no painterly microtexture, no volumetric light, no glow, no gradients, no isometric perspective. No UI, text, labels, borders or decorative presentation frame. Beautiful SIMPLE native-looking pixel art that a small beginner team can build by reusing a handful of tiles, not HD concept painting or AI photo converted to pixel effect.

scope: Visual reference only, not runtime atlas or navigation
